subcomponents.title: Uses scene-kit APIs without bypassing or duplicating them

criteria.rationale: Talk.tsx renders the kit's Presentation with steps, title, initialMode and className. Every step is built with the kit's Step type (id, era, title, caption, groupKey, Scene, payload). The shared StoryScene is typed with the kit's SceneProps and composes the kit's SceneLayer, Appear, Box, Label, Arrow, Frame and SymbolChip. The demo does not reimplement layout, motion or navigation. Presentation.tsx wires nav, Header, Stage, Toc and Footer, and Stage.tsx renders Scene with the step payload. primitives.tsx Node supplies the layoutId and layout props, and the demo supplies only identity strings and class names.
evidence: Talk.tsx returns <Presentation steps={STEPS} title=... initialMode="browse" className="story" />
steps/index.ts: STEPS maps the outline to Step<readonly Entity[]> objects with groupKey 'story', Scene: StoryScene and payload: sceneStates[i]
StoryScene.tsx imports Box, Label, Arrow, Frame, SymbolChip, SceneLayer, Appear and SceneProps from presentation-kit and picks a kit primitive per entity kind
Presentation.tsx wires validateSteps, usePresentationNav, Header, Stage, Toc and Footer; Stage.tsx renders <Scene payload={payload} />
judging basis: consensus-pass

subcomponents.title: Uses stable identities and appropriate grouped-scene architecture

criteria.rationale: Grouping: steps/index.ts creates all nine steps in a single outline.map with groupKey 'story' and the same StoryScene component. Stage.tsx keys its one motion.div by step.groupKey ?? step.id, so adjacent steps keep the same mounted scene and only the payload prop changes. A single shared groupKey is correct for one continuously evolving scene. Identity: entities.ts owns entityId(name) and a fixed name per entity. sceneStates is cumulative (additions.slice(0, i+1).flat()), so an entity keeps the same name across steps. StoryScene passes identity={entityId(entity.name)} to a kit primitive, and Box, Label, Arrow, Frame and SymbolChip all delegate to Node. Node forwards identity to motion.div as layout and layoutId, inside the LayoutGroup in Stage.tsx. Entities with the same id in consecutive steps therefore animate from old state to new state in place. Every entity kind, including connections and arrows, is rendered through this path.
evidence: steps/index.ts: STEPS = outline.map(... groupKey: 'story', Scene: StoryScene, payload: sceneStates[i]) covers all nine outline entries
Stage.tsx: <LayoutGroup><AnimatePresence><motion.div key={step.groupKey ?? step.id}> wraps <Scene payload={payload} />
entities.ts: entityId = name => `how-to-make-a-presentation:${name}`; sceneStates is cumulative
StoryScene.tsx: <Primitive identity={entityId(entity.name)} ...> keyed by entity.name on Appear
primitives.tsx Node: <motion.div layout layoutId={identity} data-presentation-entity={identity}>
Box.tsx, Label.tsx, Arrow.tsx, Frame.tsx and SymbolChip.tsx each render Node with props spread, so identity reaches Node
judging basis: consensus-pass

subcomponents.title: Maintains clear boundaries and scope discipline

criteria.rationale: Source is split cleanly. The registry (src/presentations/index.ts) holds slug and title. Talk.tsx is a thin boundary that passes steps, title, initialMode and className to the shared Presentation. Presentation-local data (entities.ts), step definitions (steps/index.ts) and scene rendering (steps/StoryScene.tsx) are separate. Shared kit code contains no demo-specific logic. The title contract is consumed: Talk passes title, and Presentation.tsx forwards it to the main element's aria-label. The registry title is a separate field. The previous audit's open question was whether ENTER_DELAY and ENTER_T in constants.ts are dead. They are not. nodes/Appear.tsx imports both from '../constants' and uses them in its motion.div transition ({ delay: ENTER_DELAY, duration: ENTER_T }), and StoryScene renders Appear for every entity. The other constants are used too: DESIGN_W, DESIGN_H and STAGE_LAYOUT in useFitScale.ts and Stage.tsx, MIN_SCALE in useFitScale.ts, and EASE and LAYOUT_T in Stage.tsx and nodes/primitives.tsx. The other public inputs are consumed: brand is rendered in Header, className lands on main, and initialMode seeds usePresentationNav. Every field of Entity (name, label, detail, x, y, w, h, kind) is read in StoryScene, and entityId is used for the Primitive identity prop. I found no dead contract or duplicated shared mechanism.

votes.rationale: Grouping: steps/index.ts creates all nine steps in a single outline.map with groupKey 'story' and the same StoryScene component. Stage.tsx keys its one motion.div by step.groupKey ?? step.id, so adjacent steps keep the same mounted scene and only the payload prop changes. A single shared groupKey is correct for one continuously evolving scene. Identity: entities.ts owns entityId(name) and a fixed name per entity. sceneStates is cumulative (additions.slice(0, i+1).flat()), so an entity keeps the same name across steps. StoryScene passes identity={entityId(entity.name)} to a kit primitive, and Box, Label, Arrow, Frame and SymbolChip all delegate to Node. Node forwards identity to motion.div as layout and layoutId, inside the LayoutGroup in Stage.tsx. Entities with the same id in consecutive steps therefore animate from old state to new state in place. Every entity kind, including connections and arrows, is rendered through this path.

votes.rationale: Source is split cleanly. The registry (src/presentations/index.ts) holds slug and title. Talk.tsx is a thin boundary that passes steps, title, initialMode and className to the shared Presentation. Presentation-local data (entities.ts), step definitions (steps/index.ts) and scene rendering (steps/StoryScene.tsx) are separate. Shared kit code contains no demo-specific logic. The title contract is consumed: Talk passes title, and Presentation.tsx forwards it to the main element's aria-label. The registry title is a separate field. The previous audit's open question was whether ENTER_DELAY and ENTER_T in constants.ts are dead. They are not. nodes/Appear.tsx imports both from '../constants' and uses them in its motion.div transition ({ delay: ENTER_DELAY, duration: ENTER_T }), and StoryScene renders Appear for every entity. The other constants are used too: DESIGN_W, DESIGN_H and STAGE_LAYOUT in useFitScale.ts and Stage.tsx, MIN_SCALE in useFitScale.ts, and EASE and LAYOUT_T in Stage.tsx and nodes/primitives.tsx. The other public inputs are consumed: brand is rendered in Header, className lands on main, and initialMode seeds usePresentationNav. Every field of Entity (name, label, detail, x, y, w, h, kind) is read in StoryScene, and entityId is used for the Primitive identity prop. I found no dead contract or duplicated shared mechanism.

votes.rationale: Neither credited mechanism is present. The port is reserved by listening on port 0, reading the port, and closing the socket, so it is released before vite starts. Readiness comes from HTTP-polling `base` with fetch(). The only ownership check is `server.exitCode !== null`, sampled at the top of each loop iteration before the next request. Readiness is not taken from the child's own announcement, and polling is not raced against the child's exit event. A server already listening on that port could answer a probe before the child's exit is observed. The `--strictPort` flag alone is insufficient.

demo-integration.rationale: All nine steps come from one outline.map in steps/index.ts. Each gets groupKey 'story', Scene StoryScene, and a cumulative payload from sceneStates. Stage.tsx keys a single motion.div by step.groupKey ?? step.id, so the grouped scene stays mounted and only the payload changes. For identity, entities.ts owns entityId and fixed entity names. StoryScene passes identity={entityId(entity.name)} to Box, Label, Arrow, Frame or SymbolChip. Each of those renders Node, which sets layout and layoutId={identity} on a motion.div inside Stage's LayoutGroup. Entities that share a name across consecutive steps therefore keep the same layoutId. All nine steps are covered because they are generated in one place. A single shared groupKey is correct for this scene.

lines.text: Unresolved-decision count: **2**. Known limitation: readability concern at 390 px is reported as P2; no physical-device or viewport matrix was tested. Risky/notable assumptions from the supplied implementation session report:
- **Risky — fit-scale bounds and chrome reservations:** small viewports can collapse the diagram and large ones can leave whitespace; the current narrow readability concern demonstrates the risk.
- **Risky — local sample colors/type/fixed coordinates:** these avoid external assets but do not establish visual readability; this round observed the narrow label-size problem.

- **Risky — targeted fault reruns:** narrowing reruns can leave current-code fault branches unsupported; implementor reported that the earlier shortfall was corrected with all eight current-code fault cases.
- **Notable — swipe and ToC thresholds:** 40 px horizontal swipe threshold and 1200 px ToC breakpoint may affect usability; a synthesized swipe worked, but no exhaustive device matrix was run.

- **Notable — screenshot naming/850 ms settle:** longer custom animations could still be unsettled and repeat runs overwrite artifacts; the sample transitions settled, custom longer animations were not tried.
## Required retests from round 0

1. **Prior P1 reproduction (narrow scene clipping). Prediction:** At 390 × 844, scene content should have remained beyond the right edge if the previous centering issue persisted. **Observation:** AXI inspected all nine steps; each canvas rect was left=24, right=366, width=342 inside the 390 px viewport. Text ranges for the final reveal extended from x≈49 to x≈343. The prior off-screen clipping symptom is resolved. A visual check of the same narrow scene shows labels only about 3–5 px tall and unreadable at normal viewport scale; this is recorded as an active, distinct residual against AT-003.

2. **Prior P2 reproduction (false collision warning). Prediction:** The desktop inspection helper should have warned on title/Present if the prior block-box diagnostic persisted. **Observation:** `npm run inspect -- how-to-make-a-presentation` built and captured all nine steps at 850 ms settle and emitted no overlap warnings. The retained desktop captures show title and Present control separated. Prior defect is resolved.
## Exploration of the changed seams

- Stage geometry is checked across every reference step at 390 × 844. All nine canvas rectangles were x=24..366 (342 px width), and the sample was visibly composed within the viewport. Desktop first/dense/last compositions were captured by the helper. No new clipping was observed.

- Diagnostics ran against the actual sample through its project-local helper. The helper captured nine settled screenshots and emitted no false title/Present warnings. The `scripts/diagnostics.mjs` and bootstrap snapshot compare byte-identically; `src/presentation-kit/Stage.tsx` and its bootstrap copy also compare byte-identically.

- Residual usability issue: the diagram text becomes too small at 390 px width to read comfortably. Expected from test-plan AT-003: important content remains readable at narrow viewport. Observed from screenshots: 880 px design canvas is rendered at 342 px width (~0.389 scale), leaving small labels around 3–5 px. See current finding in `acceptance-findings.md`.
# Acceptance findings — create-and-scene
Tested revision: `33f790fe4b4df637a4793417e40c1d60b8cc6bd3`
## Prior findings retested
### P1 — Narrow viewport scene clipping: original defect resolved; residual readability defect remains
- **Original expected behavior:** At 390 × 844, the 880 × 380 scene scales within the viewport and remains usable.

- **Original result:** The prior off-screen overflow is resolved. On the fixed revision, all nine steps reported canvas bounds x=24..366 (width 342) within the 390 px viewport, with no right-edge overflow.

- **Residual observed:** The uniformly scaled scene is only about 0.389×. Important card labels and secondary diagram text render at roughly 3–5 px high in the narrow screenshot and are not readable at normal device scale. AT-003 explicitly expects important content to remain readable at narrow width. The canvas fits geometrically, but the sample is not usable for reading its diagram on a 390 px viewport.
- **Reproduction:** Open the sample in the production preview, resize to 390 × 844, inspect step 7 or 9, and read the card and node labels.

- **Evidence:** `acceptance-screenshots/round1-axi-narrow-dense.png`, `round1-axi-narrow-last.png`; AXI measured the fixed canvas at x=24..366 and width 342. The actual text is visually legible only as tiny marks at the saved native screenshot size.
### P2 — Helper title/Present false-positive collision: resolved
- **Expected:** Separated title text and Present control should not trigger an overlap warning.

- **Observed:** On this revision, `npm run inspect -- how-to-make-a-presentation` captured all nine settled steps and emitted no overlap warnings. The no-warning result agrees with the visible desktop compositions.

- **Evidence:** `acceptance-screenshots/round1-helper-first.png`, `round1-helper-dense.png`, `round1-helper-last.png`; project-local inspection output is in the disposable copy at `scratch/acceptance-test/repo-round1/artifacts/inspection/how-to-make-a-presentation/`.
## Current finding
### P2 — Sample diagram text is unreadable at narrow width

This residual is retained as an active finding against AT-003’s narrow-view readability expectation. The Stage change fixed clipping, but uniform fit scaling shrinks the authored 880 px composition to 342 px at 390 px viewport width. The screenshot evidence above shows card labels too small to read without zooming. Reviewer should decide whether the product needs a minimum readable scale, a different narrow-mode composition, or a stated supported-width boundary; no such boundary is currently recorded in the approved artifacts.

engineering-quality.rationale: The requirement says every selector in a presentation-owned stylesheet must be scoped under the presentation's own root class or hook, or come from a CSS module. It also says to fail on any unscoped rule. presentation.css is a plain imported stylesheet, not a CSS module. It has many top-level rules that are not nested under the root class `.story`, such as `.story-entity`, `.story-entity small`, `.story-person, .story-skill`, `.story-card` and `.story-reveal`. A shared `story-` prefix in the class name does not place a selector under the `.story` root. The 'or hook' wording offers a root hook (for example a root data attribute) as an alternative to the root class. It is not an exemption for any class the presentation names after itself. The auditor narrows the requirement to rules that restyle kit or shared hooks, but the text covers 'every selector'; kit-hook selectors are named only as something included ('including'), not as the whole scope. Nothing in the packet shows that these classes cannot be loaded globally. Since the stylesheet is not a CSS module, these unscoped global rules break the requirement as written, and the fail verdict stands.
